newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Impregilo sees better years ahead.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Impregilo sees better years ahead.

text.p: Italian construction group Impregilo expects to see slightly improved results in 1997 and a return to considerably better profit levels in 1998 and 1989, the company said in a statement.

Impregilo, which made a net profit of 11.2 billion lire ($6.7 million) in 1996 after four years of losses, said that for 1997 it expected "a slight improvement in results through higher operating margins, a lower breakeven point and lower financial costs".

The group also aimed for "strategic alliances with suitable international partners" to boost its activity in several areas of southeast Asia, Impregilo said in the statement, issued after its annual general meeting. It gave no further details.
The group also wanted to develop new techniques such as project financing and activities which were complementary to its core business, like urban water and waste management services.
Impregilo said that in the first five months of this year it had won new orders worth around 1.3 trillion lire, including a contract to rebuild the burned out La Fenice theatre in Venice.
Against the background of a continuing difficult market, especially in Italy, it noted that consolidated revenues in the first quarter of this year totalled some 600 billion lire.
In line with the group's three-year plan, 1998 and 1999 will be years marking "the return to much more significant profit levels" allowing the group to expand and develop, Impregilo said.
